title: Route-centric probeboard and cost attribution for embeddings + rerank endpoints
creator: Aria Chen
description: Goal: Build a route-centric observability surface for embeddings + rerank endpoints that makes it trivial to answer: (1) why did latency spike for 'route=X'?, (2) which routes are the most expensive per-customer/per-request, and (3) are quality regressions correlated with model variants or infrastructure changes. Deliverables: (A) Probeboard: a lightweight synthetic-probing framework that runs route-level synthetic requests and captures latency, token counts, embedding sizes, cache hit rates, and end-to-end traces; (B) Cost model and per-route chargeback dashboard showing amortized GPU time, KV cache benefits, and token/embedding unit breakdown; (C) Distributed tracing integration that links frontend request IDs -> router -> GPU workers -> rerank scorer with route tags, sampled payloads, and span-level resource counters; (D) Alerting runbooks and SLO checks specific to rerank relevance and embed latency. The work focuses on hosted + dedicated deployments and on the route abstraction used by customers. Out of scope: full billing export changes, deep ML model evaluation (we'll surface regressions but not run model retraining), and on-prem private deployment integrations for this iteration.
updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design. Agreed on scope: per-route dashboards + synthetic probe runner + cost attribution prototype. Noted risk: tracing must cross process boundaries between router and GPU pool processes.

2025-02-22: Spike complete. Implemented PoC trace propagation using X-Redwood-Trace header and small shim in the router. Observed 0.8ms median overhead on path without sampling. Decided to adopt 1% full-trace sampling and 100% span-level counters for metrics aggregation.

2025-02-26: Cost model draft landed in repo (docs + calculators). We attribute cost to routes by combining per-request GPU-time samples, amortized batch size, and KV cache hit/size metrics. Early tests show embedding-heavy routes dominated cost by vector dims and batch inefficiencies.

2025-03-01: Created initial Dashboards in Datadog: 'Embed-Rerank Probeboard Overview' and 'Per-Route Cost Breakdown (Embeddings)'. Dashboard templates saved under /dashboards/embed_rerank/probeboard. Feedback from SRE: traces need better tagging for worker shard id and quantization variant.

2025-03-04: Security review triage - no user data retention beyond short-lived sample store. Added mask rule for sampled payloads. Decided to store only vector sizes and token counts; sample payloads will be redacted. Next: implement rate-limited sampling and expose metrics to Console.

Engineering notes: Trade-offs considered: (a) Full 100% tracing gives best fidelity but huge storage + cost — rejected; (b) 1% full trace + 100% lightweight counters gives good signal with bounded cost — chosen; (c) Pull-based cost attribution vs push-based per-request logging: push-based simpler for attribution but higher write volume; we will use sampled push for traces and aggregated push for counters.
Blocked items: Need dedicated metric (gpu_time_ms) emitted from the GPU runtime (dependency ENG-84500). Also waiting on tagging addition in router (ENG-43321) to attach route id to worker spans.
acceptance_criteria: Probeboard can run synthetic checks for 50 routes and produce per-route metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, embedding dims, avg batch size, kv_cache_hit_rate
Datadog dashboards exist with per-route cost slices and a summary widget for top-10 cost contributors
Traces link end-to-end with X-Redwood-Trace header; sampled full traces include route_id, model_variant, worker_shard, and gpu_time_ms
Alerting: firing rule for per-route p95 latency > 2x baseline for 15m and for per-route cost increase > 30% week-over-week
Documentation: README + runbook checked into Confluence and linked from Console; runbook includes mitigation steps and owner assignments
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Trace and sample storage costs could escalate. Mitigation: cap full trace retention to 7 days and limit to 1% sampling by default; provide controls in Console for rate adjustments.

Risk: Attribution model might double-count shared batching efficiency. Mitigation: compute amortized per-request GPU-time by dividing batch GPU time by observed batch size distribution and attribute proportionally by token/embedding weight.
Risk: Sensitive payloads in sampled traces. Mitigation: implement redaction and schema-based scrubber; avoid storing raw texts and vectors beyond size/shape metadata.
implementation_notes: Trace header: X-Redwood-Trace (UUID) propagated across frontend -> router -> worker. Router will inject route_id and model_variant into root span.
Metric names: embed.rerank.gpu_time_ms, embed.rerank.kv_cache_hit, embed.rerank.batch_size, embed.rerank.embedding_dims
Sampling: 1% full-trace sampling for heavy debugging; 100% span counters emitted as metrics with aggregation tags (route, model_variant, region)

Probeboard: lightweight runner implemented as a periodic job in infra that hits route endpoints with canonical inputs pulled from customer-provided example sets (or synthetic templates). Results stored in time-series DB and fed to dashboard.
Cost calc: GPU-minute price uses reserved/dedicated weights and is multiplied by summed gpu_time_ms for sampled intervals then normalized by requests using sampling-corrected estimators.
next_steps: Wire up gpu_time_ms emission in runtime (ENG-84500) - owner: runtime team
Add route tagging in router and release a minor bump (ENG-43321) - owner: router team
Implement sampling redaction pipeline and land scrubber in infra PR
Rollout Probeboard to staging and run 2-week collection; calibrate cost model and adjust sampling rates
Expose per-route cost widget in Console beta for selected customers
